subject: Civil Engineering
title: Geopolymer Concrete: No Cement Needed
description: A micro-lesson that makes Geopolymer Concrete: No Cement Needed usable.

hook.text: What if you could make concrete without Portland cement — and cut CO₂ by 80%?

buildup.text: Geopolymer concrete uses fly ash or slag activated by alkaline solutions instead of cement.

discovery.text: The alkaline activator triggers polymerization — forming a ceramic-like binder.

twist.text: It resists acid, fire, and sulfate attack better than Portland cement concrete.

climax.text: Australia built the first geopolymer concrete airport pavement in 2014 — it's still perfect.

punchline.text: Concrete without cement. The greenest revolution in building materials is here.

quiz.question: What replaces Portland cement in geopolymer concrete?
options: Recycled plastic granules mixed with water
Fly ash or slag activated by alkaline solutions that form a ceramic-like binder
Natural limestone ground into fine powder and mixed with sand
